args.query:
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS measurements_normalized (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  session_id TEXT,
  participant_id TEXT,
  condition TEXT,
  recorded_at DATE,
  metric_name TEXT,
  metric_value REAL,
  status TEXT,
  notes TEXT,
  source TEXT
);

-- Insert normalized rows by unpivoting cognitive_score and reaction_ms
INSERT INTO measurements_normalized (session_id, participant_id, condition, recorded_at, metric_name, metric_value, status, notes, source)
SELECT session_id, participant_id, condition, recorded_at, 'cognitive_score' as metric_name, cognitive_score as metric_value, status, notes,
       CASE
         WHEN lower(notes) LIKE '%rescored%' THEN 'rescored'
         WHEN lower(notes) LIKE '%original%' THEN 'original'
         ELSE NULL
       END as source
FROM measurements
UNION ALL
SELECT session_id, participant_id, condition, recorded_at, 'reaction_ms' as metric_name, reaction_ms as metric_value, status, notes,
       CASE
         WHEN lower(notes) LIKE '%rescored%' THEN 'rescored'
         WHEN lower(notes) LIKE '%original%' THEN 'original'
         ELSE NULL
       END as source
FROM measurements;
SELECT COUNT(*) as cnt FROM measurements_normalized;

Done — I created a normalized measurements table and populated it.

What I did
- Created a table measurements_normalized with columns:
  - id (autoincrement PK), session_id, participant_id, condition, recorded_at, metric_name, metric_value, status, notes, source
- Populated the table by unpivoting cognitive_score and reaction_ms from the existing measurements table (each original session row becomes two rows: one for cognitive_score, one for reaction_ms).
- For the new source column I set:
  - 'rescored' if notes contains 'rescored' (case-insensitive)
  - 'original' if notes contains 'original' (case-insensitive)
  - NULL otherwise

SQL I ran
- Create table:
  CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS measurements_normalized (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    session_id TEXT,
    participant_id TEXT,
    condition TEXT,
    recorded_at DATE,
    metric_name TEXT,
    metric_value REAL,
    status TEXT,
    notes TEXT,
    source TEXT
  );

- Insert (unpivot):
  INSERT INTO measurements_normalized (session_id, participant_id, condition, recorded_at, metric_name, metric_value, status, notes, source)
  SELECT session_id, participant_id, condition, recorded_at, 'cognitive_score' AS metric_name, cognitive_score AS metric_value, status, notes,
         CASE WHEN lower(notes) LIKE '%rescored%' THEN 'rescored'
              WHEN lower(notes) LIKE '%original%' THEN 'original'
              ELSE NULL END AS source
  FROM measurements
  UNION ALL
  SELECT session_id, participant_id, condition, recorded_at, 'reaction_ms' AS metric_name, reaction_ms AS metric_value, status, notes,
         CASE WHEN lower(notes) LIKE '%rescored%' THEN 'rescored'
              WHEN lower(notes) LIKE '%original%' THEN 'original'
              ELSE NULL END AS source
  FROM measurements;

Result summary
- The INSERT reported rows_affected = 54 (so 54 normalized rows were added). That corresponds to 27 original session rows unpivoted to 54 metric rows (2 metrics per session), matching the recent measurements I inspected.

Notes and next steps
